title: Kan simplicial models for arrows over the infinity category of spaces
statement: Use simplicial sets, ordinary nerves, quasicategories, coherent functor categories, mapping spaces and equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the infinity category of small spaces $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Fix nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'\in\mathcal U''$ large enough for the following categories. Let $\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U}$ be the ordinary category of $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets and let $j:N(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U})\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ be passage to the homotopy type, exhibiting spaces as its homotopy coherent localization at weak homotopy equivalences. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ be any coherent functor from an infinity category fitting in $\mathcal U'$, and form the infinity-categorical pullback $\mathcal P=N(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U})\times^h_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}\mathcal E$, with projection $r:\mathcal P\to\mathcal E$. An object of this pullback is a triple $(K,A,\alpha)$ with an equivalence $\alpha:jK\simeq pA$. For every arrow $F:A\to B$ of $\mathcal E$, there are $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes $K,L$, equivalences $\alpha:jK\simeq pA$, $\beta:jL\simeq pB$, an actual simplicial map $f:K\to L$, and an arrow $\widetilde F:(K,A,\alpha)\to(L,B,\beta)$ in $\mathcal P$ projecting to $f$ in $N(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U})$ and to the component of $F$ in $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(A,B)$. In particular, $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,r)$ is essentially surjective: every arrow of $\mathcal E$ is equivalent in its coherent arrow category to an image arrow. A Kan complex is allowed to be empty. No Cartesian-fibration hypothesis on $p$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the Kan model structure to $\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U}$. Its fibrant objects are precisely the Kan complexes, and every simplicial set is cofibrant because the map from the empty simplicial set is degreewise injective. The stipulated functor $j$ is its universal infinity localization at precisely these weak equivalences. Consequently the fibrant-representative clause of the frame lemma gives $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes $K,L$ and equivalences $\alpha:jK\simeq pA$, $\beta:jL\simeq pB$. Enlarge the ambient universe to $\mathcal U\prime$ when applying the model-category localization statement; this changes no object or simplicial-set size. This use of the localization interface does not identify an arbitrary localization functor with the coherent nerve on maps without justification.

source.place: Agent specialization of the cited model-category localization statements; Hovey Chapter 5, with infinity-localization comparison as specified in the frame node.

proof.text: In $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}(jK,jL)$ consider the component of $\beta^{-1}\circ p(F)\circ\alpha$. Apply the frame lemma with the cofibrant object $K$ and fibrant object $L$. It states that every component of this localized mapping space is represented by an actual map $K\to L$. Choose such an $f$. Thus $\beta\circ j(f)$ and $p(F)\circ\alpha$ belong to the same component of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}(jK,pB)$: composition on components is composition in the homotopy category, and $\beta\circ\beta^{-1}$ lies in the identity component. A connecting path is chosen in the next step.

source.place: Agent specialization of the actual-map representative clause of lem-coef-cosimplicial-frame-mapping.

proof.text: Use the model clause of the pullback lemma with $\mathcal A=N(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U})$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal E$, $\mathcal C=\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ and functors $j,p$: take $\mathcal P$ to be the simplicial pullback $(N(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathcal U})\times\mathcal E)\times_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\times\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}}\operatorname{Eq}(\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ and $r$ its projection to $\mathcal E$; its objects are the triples $(K,A,\alpha)$ of the statement. Since $\operatorname{Eq}$ is full in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$, an edge $(K,A,\alpha)\to(L,B,\beta)$ is a triple $(g,G,\sigma)$: an edge $g$ of the nerve, i.e. a simplicial map $K\to L$, an edge $G:A\to B$, and $\sigma:\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ with rows $\alpha$ ($t=0$), $\beta$ ($t=1$) and columns $j(g)$, $p(G)$. Its projections are $g$ and $G$ on the nose. Construct $\sigma$ for $(f,F)$. By inner horn filling choose $2$-simplices $\tau_1$ with edges $01=j(f)$, $12=\beta$, $02=c_1$ and $\tau_2$ with edges $\alpha$, $p(F)$, $c_2$. By step 2, $c_1,c_2$ lie in one component of $\operatorname{Map}(jK,pB)$, which is Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]; so there is an edge from $c_2$ to $c_1$, a $2$-simplex $\omega$ with edges $01=1_{jK}$, $02=c_2$, $12=c_1$. On vertices $jK,jK,jL,pB$ the faces $d_0=\tau_1$, $d_2=\omega$, $d_3=s_0(j(f))$ agree on common edges and form an inner horn $\Lambda^3_1$. A filler has $d_1$ with edges $j(f),\beta,c_2$. It and $\tau_2$ share the edge $c_2$ and glue to $\sigma$ on the two nondegenerate triangles of $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$. Put $\widetilde F=(f,F,\sigma)$. It projects to exactly $f$ and $F$. Accessibility, colimit and Cartesian hypotheses are not used.

source.place: Strict equivalence-arrow pullback model stated by lem-coef-accessible-pullback-filtered-colimit; inner horn filling as in HTT Definition 1.1.2.4; agent construction of the square (reviewer repair 2026-10-17).

proof.text: By step 3, $r(\widetilde F)=F$. The degenerate edge $s_0(F)$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal E)$ from $r(\widetilde F)$ to $F$ is an equivalence: it is its own inverse, both inverse equations witnessed by degenerate $2$-simplices. In particular $\widetilde F$ projects to the component of $F$, and $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,r)$ is essentially surjective. Empty Kan complexes are allowed by the Kan model structure: for $pA$ empty take $K$ empty; if $pB$ is empty the existence of $p(F)$ forces $pA$ empty as well. The construction uses no Cartesian-fibration property of $p$.
